name: Hortus Malabaricus and Itty Achuden’s contribution
description: The first volume of a Malabar botanical compilation preserves a signed statement by Ezhava physician Itty Achuden, whose knowledge contributed to a work associated with Hendrik van Rheede.

impact.note: One printed compilation that made Malabar plants known to European botanists more exactly, with later plant names and floras drawing on it.

date.basis: Date of the cited witness; not a claim of origin.

events.statement: Volume 1, dated 1678, preserves a Malayalam-script statement by Itty Achuden; the compilation also involved Dutch and other Indian contributors.

evidence.supports: The National Centre for Biological Sciences identifies Itty Achudem as an Ezhava physician and attributes a signed statement in Malayalam script to him in volume 1 of Hortus Indicus Malabaricus, dated 1678.

The article discusses van Rheede’s botanical compilation and a certificate by Ezhava physician Itty Acchudan concerning information supplied to Dutch interlocutors; other Indian experts also contributed.
Identifies van Reede’s organization, Indian expertise and multilingual mediation; says the first volume was edited without his knowledge.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest scoped witness checked here; not the origin of the wider knowledge.

caveats: This is a colonial-era collaborative publication; the 1678 witness does not establish the origin of the community’s knowledge or assign every entry to one contributor. The later historical account reports that the first volume was edited and annotated without van Reede’s knowledge; roles in collection, translation and publication were not identical.

research.note: Independent review checked NCBS’s description of the signed certificate and first-volume date, MPIWG’s colonial context and botanical contributors, and Magdalen College’s account of mediation and publication.
